      "explanation":"stolen_card",
      "likelihood":"high",
      "reasoning":"The issuing-country/IP mismatch and failed address verification support card misuse. The failed identity check strengthens that explanation, without establishing the precise fraud mechanism."
    },
    {
      "explanation":"legitimate_customer",
      "likelihood":"low",
      "reasoning":"An established-device customer shipping home could legitimately use a foreign-issued card with an address discrepancy. However, the failed identity check decides the order under policy despite that possibility."

  "disposition":"decline",
  "citations":["R03","FP-2 §6.3","FP-2 §6.4","FP-2 §6.6(b)","FP-2 §5.2","FP-2 §5.3(b)","FP-2 §4.2"],
  "next_check":"none",
  "memo":"Recommend decline. Only R03 holds, making Card the sole adverse family; no Context rule holds. Linkage conditions are absent, so household exceptions are unnecessary and escalation is prohibited. No earlier outcome settles the order. The required id_check failed, overriding the ordinary hold under §6.6(b): §5.3(b) requires decline without Linkage. A legitimate customer using a foreign-issued card remains plausible, but established-device and home-shipping facts do not override verification failure. The order is unshipped, so decline voids and refunds it and blocks the account. No further check would change the policy disposition."
